title: A Multitask, Multilingual, Multimodal Evaluation of ChatGPT on Reasoning, Hallucination, and Interactivity
venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing and the 3rd Conference of the Asia-Pacific Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
extended_summary:
This paper presents a broad benchmark framework for evaluating ChatGPT across multiple NLP capabilities, including summarization, machine translation, sentiment analysis, question answering, task-oriented dialogue, open-domain knowledge-grounded dialogue, misinformation detection, reasoning, hallucination, and multimodal generation. The authors aim to move beyond anecdotal reports by systematically testing the model’s strengths and weaknesses using publicly available datasets and manually checked outputs.

The approach is not an educational intervention but a large-scale model evaluation. It examines ChatGPT in zero-shot settings on 21–23 datasets, with additional experiments on multilingual performance, multi-turn interaction, and code-mediated multimodal generation. The evaluation includes languages spanning high-, medium-, low-, and extremely low-resource categories, and it assesses reasoning across deductive, inductive, abductive, mathematical, temporal, spatial, commonsense, causal, multi-hop, and analogical categories.

The paper concludes that ChatGPT performs strongly on many tasks in zero-shot settings and can sometimes match or exceed fine-tuned models, but it remains unreliable in reasoning, weak in low-resource and non-Latin-script languages, and prone to hallucination. Multi-turn interaction can improve outputs in summarization, translation, and image-generation-by-code tasks, but the authors emphasize that ChatGPT’s capabilities are inconsistent and far from comprehensive.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI system based on a GPT-family large language model, fine-tuned for dialogue and interactive text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper benchmarks ChatGPT on multitask NLP, multilingual understanding and translation, multimodal code-based image generation, reasoning, factuality/hallucination, and multi-turn interactivity.

findings.finding_summary: On 9/13 NLP datasets with reported zero-shot LLM baselines, ChatGPT outperformed previous zero-shot LLMs. The paper also reports that it outperformed fully fine-tuned task-specific models on 4 tasks, though it lagged behind task-specific fully fine-tuned models in most settings.
findings.measure: Task performance across summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, QA, misinformation detection, dialogue, and knowledge-grounded dialogue
findings.sample_size: subsets of 30 to 200 samples per task

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT showed stronger performance on high-resource languages and weaker performance on low-resource and extremely low-resource languages. For sentiment analysis and language identification, it achieved 84% accuracy on English, 80% on Indonesian, 78% on Javanese, and 56% on Buginese; for language identification the corresponding accuracies were 100%, 100%, 0%, and 12%.
findings.measure: Accuracy on sentiment analysis and language identification
findings.sample_size: 4 languages; n not clearly reported in the table excerpt

findings.finding_summary: In machine translation, performance was substantially better for high-resource languages than for low-resource languages. The paper reports 24/30 and 29/30 correct XXXEng translations for Chinese and French, versus 7/30 and 9/30 for Javanese and Sundanese; for EngXXX translation, the low-resource languages again performed poorly (6/30 and 0/30).

The paper reports that ChatGPT's reasoning performance was uneven: it was stronger on deduction than induction, weaker on mathematical and spatial reasoning, and relatively strong on commonsense and temporal reasoning. For example, it scored 23.33% (7/30) on MATH, 26/30 on timedial, and 43.33% and 43.75% on StepGame and SpartQA respectively.
findings.sample_size: Multiple benchmarks; typically n=30 per task, MATH n not explicitly stated in excerpt

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT suffered from hallucination across tasks, especially extrinsic hallucinations in generation settings. The paper states that hallucination was observed in machine translation and QA, while intrinsic hallucinations were rare in summarization and knowledge-grounded open-domain dialogue.

Interactive multi-turn prompting improved performance. The paper reports gains of 7.99 ROUGE-1 and 1.64 ROUGE-2 on summarization, and 2% ChrF++ on low-resource machine translation, with 34% of samples improving from turn 1 to 2 and 36% from turn 2 to 3 in the flag-drawing task.
findings.measure: ROUGE-1/ROUGE-2, ChrF++, and flag-drawing error grades across turns
findings.sample_size: 50 SAMSum documents; 50 national flags; MT sample size adapted from translation subset

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark-style empirical paper, but it is not a controlled educational study and does not evaluate K-12 learners or instructional outcomes. The evidence is useful for understanding model capabilities, yet the methodology is heterogeneous and not designed for causal inference in education.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful performance differences on several NLP tasks, including clear weaknesses on low-resource languages and gains from interactivity. However, it does not provide educational effect sizes for K-12 literacy outcomes, so direct instructional impact remains unclear.
